## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

HOW to create repo on github

```{On that blue Quick setup box, click the link “uploading an existing file” (it’s right after “creating a new file”).}

Drag in your three files:

app.py (you can rename your piece_of_advice_app.py to app.py before uploading)

requirements.txt (contents: streamlit>=1.36)

advice_data.json

Add a commit message → Commit changes.

Or make the button appear

Click creating a new file → name it README.md → put any text → Commit.

Now you’ll see the file list. At the top right (above the list, next to the green Code button) there’s a dropdown Add file → Upload files. Use that to upload the 3 files.

Once the files are in the repo, you can deploy on Streamlit Cloud: New app → pick the repo → set App file to app.py → Deploy.
```

DEPLOY in streamlit

```{Deploy to Streamlit Community Cloud (easiest)}

Go to streamlit.io/cloud and sign in with GitHub.

Click New app.

Pick your repo: krisauw / a_piece_of_advice, branch main.

App file: app.py.

Leave the rest as defaults (it will install from requirements.txt).

Click Deploy.
You’ll get a public URL in a minute. Any push to GitHub will auto-redeploy (if you add libraries, update requirements.txt).

Run locally (for testing)
# from your project folder
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/Scripts/activate   # Windows
pip install -r requirements.txt
streamlit run app.py

Common gotchas

Keep advice_data.json in the same folder as app.py (you already did).

If the build fails, open the app’s Logs in Streamlit Cloud—errors usually point to a missing package or wrong file path.
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
